content:
The [Robots.txt Generator](/robots-txt-generator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Build a robots.txt file — allow and disallow rules, plus your sitemap. Enter your user-agent ( * for all crawlers ) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Build a robots.txt file without writing it by hand: add allow and disallow rules for the crawlers you care about, add your sitemap address, and copy the finished file to your site's root. A robots.txt tells search engines which parts of your site they may crawl — it is a request, not a lock, but every major crawler honours it. Everything runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Robots.txt Generator

Start by typing or pasting your user-agent ( * for all crawlers ). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Add the paths you want to block (Disallow) and the ones to explicitly allow (Allow).
2. Add your sitemap URL if you have one.
3. Copy the generated robots.txt and save it as robots.txt at your site's root.

## How it works

The [Robots.txt Generator](/robots-txt-generator) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Disallowing /admin/ and /search/ for all crawlers, with a sitemap line, produces a robots.txt with `User-agent: *`, two `Disallow:` lines and a `Sitemap:` line. Try the same figures in the [Robots.txt Generator](/robots-txt-generator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Robots.txt Generator](/robots-txt-generator) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What robots.txt does — and does not do

It asks well-behaved crawlers (Google, Bing and the rest) to skip the paths you list. It does not hide those pages: anyone who knows the address can still visit them, and a page that is linked from elsewhere can still be indexed without being crawled. For pages that must stay private, use a password or a noindex tag instead.

## Common mistakes

Blocking the whole site (`Disallow: /`) by accident is the classic one — check the generated file before uploading it. Blocking CSS and JavaScript files is another: search engines need them to render your pages properly. And a robots.txt belongs at the root of the site (example.com/robots.txt), nowhere else.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Always add a Sitemap line — it is the easiest way to make sure crawlers find your sitemap.
- Block admin, search-result and duplicate pages; leave CSS and JavaScript alone.
- Check the file with the Robots.txt Checker after uploading it.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is robots.txt?

A small text file at the root of a website that tells search engine crawlers which pages they may and may not visit. It starts with a User-agent line, then Allow and Disallow rules. Try it with your own numbers in the [Robots.txt Generator](/robots-txt-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does robots.txt hide pages from Google?

No — it only asks crawlers not to visit them. A page that is linked from elsewhere can still be indexed. Use noindex or a password for pages that must stay private. Try it with your own numbers in the [Robots.txt Generator](/robots-txt-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Where does robots.txt go?

At the root of the site — example.com/robots.txt. Anywhere else, crawlers will not find it. Try it with your own numbers in the [Robots.txt Generator](/robots-txt-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What do I need to use the Robots.txt Generator?

Just User-agent ( * for all crawlers ). Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
